title: LEF1 regulated CTHRC1 promotes silica-induced pulmonary fibrosis through CD44-dependent signaling.
authors: Wang, Ting; Sun, Wenqing; Yang, Qingyan; Jia, Xinying; Lian, Wenxiu; Meng, Fanqing; Chen, Jingyu; Xu, Shangcheng; Liu, Yi; Ni, Chunhui
one_liner_zh: 该文研究LEF1转录因子结合CTHRC1启动子及CTHRC1-CD44互作在矽肺纤维化中的作用，虽涉及TF-DNA结合和AlphaFold2结构预测，但核心为疾病机制而非TF-DNA互作建模，方法上AI/物理模拟仅作辅助验证。
abstract: Silicosis is an incurable fibrotic lung disease caused by crystalline silica exposure. Aberrant activation of lung fibroblasts into pathological fibroblasts is a hallmark of silicosis. CTHRC1 has been considered a novel fibroblast activation biomarker. This study sought to explore CTHRC1's role in silicosis and determine the signaling pathways it modulates. A combination of transcriptomic analysis of clinical samples, LC-MS/MS, Co-IP, and cationic nanoliposome-based techniques was utilized. In vitro models of lung fibroblast activation induced by TGF-beta1, PDGF or recombinant CTHRC1 (rCTHRC1), as well as in vivo models of pulmonary fibrosis induced by silica or bleomycin in mice were established. RNA sequencing, Western blot, RT-qPCR, AlphaFold2 analyses and rescue experiments using siCTHRC1, siCD44, CTHRC1 plasmids, and the PI3K activator 740 Y-P were performed to explore the underlying mechanisms. CTHRC1 is a significantly dysregulated gene implicated in myogenesis and ECM-related pathways. Mechanistically, lymphoid enhancer-binding factor 1 (LEF1) exerts its transcriptional regulator role by binding to the CTHRC1 promoter region in TGF-beta1-activated fibroblasts. Further, CTHRC1 mediates its pro-fibroblast-to-myofibroblast transition function by directly binding to the CD44 receptor. AlphaFold2 analyses revealed the binding between CTHRC1 and CD44 is accomplished by three critical CD44 residues: Arg41, Asn172, and Trp650. Rescue experiments demonstrated that the CTHRC1-CD44 complex exerts its pro-fibrotic effects through AKT signaling. In vivo, liposomal Cthrc1 siRNA mitigated fibrogenesis in both silica- and bleomycin-induced mouse fibrosis models. Our results uncover a previously unrecognized role of the LEF1-CTHRC1-CD44 axis in silicosis and highlight the therapeutic target potential of CTHRC1 in fibrotic lung diseases.
abstract_zh: 矽肺是一种由结晶二氧化硅暴露引起的不可治愈的纤维化肺部疾病。肺成纤维细胞异常激活为病理性成纤维细胞是矽肺的一个标志。CTHRC1已被认为是一种新型的成纤维细胞激活生物标志物。本研究旨在探讨CTHRC1在矽肺中的作用，并确定其调控的信号通路。研究采用了临床样本的转录组学分析、LC-MS/MS、Co-IP以及阳离子纳米脂质体技术的组合。建立了由TGF-beta1、PDGF或重组CTHRC1 (rCTHRC1)诱导的肺成纤维细胞激活的体外模型，以及由二氧化硅或博来霉素诱导的小鼠肺纤维化体内模型。通过RNA测序、Western blot、RT-qPCR、AlphaFold2分析以及使用siCTHRC1、siCD44、CTHRC1质粒和PI3K激活剂740 Y-P的拯救实验，探讨了潜在机制。CTHRC1是一个显著失调的基因，涉及肌生成和ECM相关通路。机制上，淋巴增强子结合因子1 (LEF1)通过结合TGF-beta1激活的成纤维细胞中CTHRC1启动子区域发挥其转录调控作用。进一步，CTHRC1通过直接结合CD44受体介导其促成纤维细胞向肌成纤维细胞转化的功能。AlphaFold2分析揭示了CTHRC1与CD44之间的结合由三个关键CD44残基完成：Arg41、Asn172和Trp650。拯救实验表明，CTHRC1-CD44复合物通过AKT信号通路发挥其促纤维化作用。在体内，脂质体Cthrc1 siRNA在二氧化硅和博来霉素诱导的小鼠纤维化模型中均减轻了纤维生成。我们的结果揭示了LEF1-CTHRC1-CD44轴在矽肺中先前未被认识的作用，并强调了CTHRC1在纤维化肺部疾病中的治疗靶点潜力。
